newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schenker improves turnover, profits in '96.
newsitem.headline: Schenker improves turnover, profits in '96.

text.p: Global freight forwarder Schenker International expects to increase 1996 air and sea freight turnover to 3.3 billion marks from 3.29 billion marks last year, parent company Stinnes AG said.
Schenker International had defended its leading position this year and would improve turnover and profits substantially, Stinnes chairman Helmut Mamsch told a news briefing.
In Germany, the forwarder has successfully integrated Rhenus Air International and extended co-operation with large clients, he said according to a copy of his speech provided to Reuters.
The two ambitious logistics projects for Siemens AG semi-conductor factories in Dresden and Newcastle were making good progress, he added.

But the Schenker International European subsidiaries, especially Italy, Sweden and France, suffered considerable falls in air cargo tonnage and their results remained below their traditional good level, Mamsch said.
In the U.S., a restructuring, new management and expansion of sales outlets allowed Schenker International to achieve a financial turnaround, he added.
Subsidiaries in Asia, especially Australia, Hong Kong and China, had improved their financial results considerably, Mamsch said.
The merger of Schenker and Rhenus into the new transport parent company Schenker-Rhenus AG at the start of 1996 had improved the competitiveness of the transport division substantially, he said.
"This year we achieved the turn-around in the transport field. The transport and logistics market is, and remains a growth market with satisfactory growth rates," he added.
The Stinnes transport division expected turnover of 7.9 billion marks this year compared to 8.2 billion marks in 1995.
Schenker Eurocargo, responsible for European road transport, expected turnover of 3.03 billion marks this year from 3.19 billion marks in 1995.
